messages:
release-bot: ALERT: canary group inference-canary-3 exceeded abort thresholds at 1876543210 — 5xx rate 12% (SLO breach threshold=8%), healthcheck flapping detected. Abort criteria triggered automatically. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/canary/inference-canary-3

pagerduty: Paging @Alex Cheng (oncall) and @Priya Nair (secondary). Escalation policy: canary-failure -> eng-oncall -> oncall-sre.

Alex Cheng: On it. Joining signal channel. Can anyone confirm which rollout this canary is for? quick context pls. :eyes:

Taylor (releases): This was rollout r2026.03.15-067 — model routing + small config tweak for KV cache sizing. Targeted 10% of traffic to model_v2.

Priya Nair: Seeing the same in logs. Example from proxy logs: ``[2026-03-15T17:20:05Z] inference-canary-3 svc=inference route=/v1/gen status=502 latency=120ms``. Also health probe failures: ``/health -> 504`` intermittently.

Erin S: Reproduced an occurance locally against canary variant — connection resets when sequence length > 1024. Might be a model runtime degenerate path.

Alex Cheng: Ok, abort criteria already triggered but we need manual mitigation: options are (1) flip feature flag to stop routing to v2, (2) abort rollout / rollback to prev revision, (3) scale up canary pool. What’s fastest?

Taylor (releases): Fastest is feature flag kill-switch. I can flip it in LaunchCtrl. Command: ``ffctl toggle --env prod model_v2_routing false``. That will reduce traffic immediately. If that doesn't settle errors we should rollback.

Miguel O: I'll watch the control plane and prepare rollback command. Pre-staging checks passed earlier but looks like runtime edge-case.

Priya Nair: Initiating FF toggle now.

Priya Nair: ``ffctl toggle --env prod model_v2_routing false`` -> ok:returned 200. TTL 0s. Rolling out kill-switch :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Feature flag model_v2_routing set to false for environment prod by Priya Nair. Impact: Canary routing reduced to 0% within ~10s.

Alex Cheng: Monitoring metrics. Can someone paste the 5xx graph short link?

Priya Nair: Shortlink: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/canary/inference-canary-3?view=5m — 5xx dropped from 12% -> 1.1% within 45s. Healthchecks stabilized.

Taylor (releases): Good. Callout: because we toggled the flag the global rollout is paused. I'll keep the rollout paused and create a rollback if needed.

Erin S: I still see a few sporadic 502s from older canary pods; likely draining. Error volume within acceptable customer impact window. No customer-facing alerts triggered by monitoring.

Alex Cheng: Quick customer-impact summary for incident ticket: - Affected surface: 10% of inference traffic (canary) for ~12 minutes - Elevated 5xx peaked at 12% then dropped below 2% after kill-switch - Partial degradation for small subset of requests; no broad outage - No mitigation required by customer side.

Taylor (releases): I'll run a rollback to previous deployment revision for the canary group to be safe. Command I'll run: ``kubectl -n inference rollout undo deploy/inference-service --to-revision=48``. Miguel, please watch for rollout progress.

Miguel O: Watching. Pre-rollout: 3/3 old pods ready, 2/3 new pods flapping. Issuing rollback now.

Miguel O: Rollback in progress — new pods terminating, old revision replica count increasing. Logs: ``rolled back to revision 48``.

ops-bot: Rollback complete. All canary pods running revision 48. Healthchecks OK.

Priya Nair: Re-enabled telemetry checks. All synthetic tests green after rollback + flag off.

Alex Cheng: Thanks team. I'm escalating to SRE-ML for root cause analysis (possible runtime regression with long sequences). Taylor please open an incident ticket and link to rollout artifacts.

Taylor (releases): Filed INC-1942: "Canary: model_v2 runtime 5xx on long sequences" — includes links: deployment config, ff toggle audit, grafana graphs, kube events, and logs. Assigned to @Erin S and @Miguel O for RCA.

Erin S: I'll start a bisect on the model runtime changes and reproduce a minimal repro. Initial hypothesis: KV cache change + attention kernel ordering causing rare OOB on long sequences.

Alex Cheng: Handoff to next on-call @Priya Nair for follow-ups. Priya — action items: monitor the RCA thread, validate any hotfix before unpausing rollout, and confirm customers unaffected in 12h window.

Priya Nair: Acknowledged, taking handoff. Will keep an eye on related alerts and post an update in #incidents in 2h or earlier if anything flares.

pagerduty: Incident INC-1942 created and assigned. Severity: sev2. First response time: 90s.

Alex Cheng: Closing coordination in this thread. We'll keep the incident ticket open for the RCA. If anyone sees residual errors, ping pagerduty. Thanks all. :tada:
